raw_response:
Let me think through this year the way I always do.

---

*Me and my old man, we farm these 7 mu same as we have for years. The kids are gone to the city, so it's just the two of us now. I'm 69, he's not young either. I don't read, I never went to school, but I've put seed in this ground for 47 years and I know what it wants.*

**Wheat.** I'll put it in after the maize comes out in October, like always. First I'll have the machine man come rotary-till the stubble — costs some money but at my age I'm not turning soil by hand. I buy the seed at the shop in town, the regular kind, about 25-26 jin per mu, drilled with the hired planter. Before planting I spread about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the white-bag 15-15-15 kind everyone uses. Then when the wheat turns green after winter, I walk the field and spread urea by hand, a bit less than a bag per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I put a little more, if it looks strong I save a handful. I don't measure with scales, I know by feel how heavy the bucket should be.

I water three times — once before the ground freezes hard, once at green-up when the spring comes, and once when the heads are filling if May is dry. The well is ours, but the electric costs money so I don't water more than I have to. Last year the neighbor Mrs. Wang watered only twice and her wheat was fine, but my field is drier on the west side, so three is safer for me.

Herbicide I spray in spring, can't stand weeds in wheat. If the aphids come at heading I'll have my nephew come with his sprayer and hit it once. Harvest I hire the combine — everyone in the village shares the same harvest man, he does all our fields in two days. I expect about 800-some jin per mu, that's what I get most years.

**Maize.** Soon as the wheat is off in June, the planter comes right behind and drops maize seed into the stubble — no tilling, no time for it anyway. The window is only a few days, if rain comes you're stuck. I buy hybrid seed, the shopkeeper tells me which one everyone's planting this year. I put compound fertilizer down with the planter, then walk the rows at knee-high to spread urea at the base of each plant — tiring work but it matters.

Maize I usually don't water unless July is dry, the summer rains mostly take care of it. One spray for the weeds when the plants are small. Then I wait — maize is the easy crop, it mostly grows itself if the rain cooperates. Harvest is September, combine again. Get around 900 jin per mu in a normal year.

**What I can't do.** I can't afford to gamble on anything new, and I don't have the strength for extra work. My son sends money sometimes but I keep the farm paying for itself. I do what I did last year and the year before. If something works, you don't change it.
